implementation.compatibility_classification: IBM TSO/E and VM non-SAA built-in.
implementation.approach: Reuses rexx_builtin_next_word, the bounded byte-oriented scanner already used by SPACE; counts content and gaps, computes a virtual SPACE-normalized prefix, and writes once through the existing result allocator. No intermediate normalized string or second tokenizer.
implementation.normalization: Existing SPACE blank class: ASCII space and bytes tab through carriage return. Trims leading/trailing blanks and collapses blank runs.
implementation.truncation: Right-truncates the normalized view to length and removes a final normalized separator before counting surviving words and gaps.
implementation.padding: For multiple remaining words, preserves each original normalized gap and distributes added width by quotient/remainder; remainder bytes go to gaps from left to right. The exactly-one-byte pad replaces separators and may be NUL.
implementation.empty_single_word_and_zero_width: Empty/all-blank values remain empty. A single word is not extended outside itself; it is unchanged if it fits and right-truncated if it does not. Width zero returns the empty prefix. These follow IBM's documented between-word padding and truncation rules; the IBM examples do not list each edge as a standalone vector.
implementation.limits: Byte-oriented; embedded NUL and high-bit bytes are preserved. Existing whole-number parsing and 16 MiB runtime output limit are retained. No Unicode, DBCS, locale, or transcoding behavior is claimed.
